question: Can the actual low-power Fig3c processed magnitude be pointwise inverted using the independently published central ideal hanger rates, without clipping, fitting or silently ignoring measurement effects?

output.domain: One exposed low-power Set III processed experimental curve; not raw complex time records or all source data
output.accuracy: Exact rational comparisons of preserved decimal tokens against rounded central rates; no physical uncertainty threshold

model.assumptions: Conditional real-deembedded stationary passive single-pole transfer. Central lower amplitude bound kappa_int/(kappa_int+kappa_ext), upper finite-inverse boundary 1. Gain-only diagnostic relaxes to closed range [l,1] with independently variable latent amplitudes and one common positive gain; compatibility is only necessary.
model.approximation: Ideal transfer not admitted as exact measurement operator. Noise, complex mismatch and averaging cannot be silently dropped; outside-domain counts do not reject physics.
model.initial_boundary: Authors classify Fig3c as a single stable fixed-point regime; per-record stationarity/averaging bounds remain unresolved.
model.drive_environment: Low-power nominal single-power sweep per source. Absolute flux and Kerr not inferred or used in this dimensionless domain profile.
model.parameters: Set III linewidths from independently determined source Table1, rounded central 0.68 and 1.64 MHz in frequency-over-2pi units. Common conversion cancels; no target-derived gain adopted as calibration, selected branch or physical calibration uncertainty invented. Envelope optimizer is a diagnostic certificate, not a correction.
